name: Kaladatta
bloodline: Datta (hereditary stonemason lineage, serving the Mauryan court)
residence: Kumrahar Quarter (Stoneworkers' precinct near the Great Assembly Hall)
daily_routine: inspecting the integrity of palace pillars and the Great Hall
repairing cracks in stone and fired-brick foundations
maintaining the assembly plaza and processional pathways
studying wear patterns in the older wooden-palisade sections
coordinating labor for heavy stonework and pillar transport
monitoring structural shifts after the monsoon rains
cataloging reused, replaced, or re-dressed stone blocks

goals.public_goal: Maintain the structural integrity of the palace complex, prevent collapse or degradation of the Great Hall and ramparts, and ensure safe use of the plaza and shrine infrastructure
goals.hidden_goal: Identify the original construction phases of the palace-monument complex and separate the old wooden-palisade work, the brick-era additions, and the later polished Chunar-stone work from one another
goals.deep_goal: Understand whether different sections of the complex were built under different rulers, by different methods, or by different hands entirely

beliefs: Stone and timber preserve truth better than court chronicles
Most mysteries are just misunderstood construction layers
Reused stone tells a history people forget to read
Structural anomalies matter more than palace legends
The complex is not a single monument, but a layered system built across generations
